title: operator-session-attestation: consent-gated KMS routing and RBACv2 enforcement migration tooling
author: Lena Morales
release_notes: Adds attested operator-session binding to per-request audit stamps, introduces consent-gated KMS routing with local-region preference and explicit multi-region fallback, and provides RBACv2 shadow->enforce migration helpers and validation tooling.
description:
Context and motivation: customers with strict residency and key locality requirements asked for clearer proof that operator actions (human or operator service) are both authorized and pinned to the expected KMS scope. This PR implements a two-part solution: (1) a cryptographic per-request audit "presence stamp" that binds request id, operator-session lease id, and the KMS key id used for the operation; and (2) consent-gated routing for KMS operations that prefers tenant-local keys but can fall back to a multi-region key path only if an explicit tenant consent claim is present. Additionally, to unblock rollout we add RBACv2 shadow->enforce migration utilities and an rbacctl policy validation command to reduce risk during enforcement toggles.

Checklist:
- [x] implement audit presence stamp generator and verifier
- [x] add operator-session lease propagation into request context and audit headers
- [x] implement consent-gated KMS router with region-preference and explicit-consent fallback
- [x] expose rbacctl validate and migration helpers for shadow->enforce cutover
- [x] unit and integration tests for stamp verification and fallback logic
- [x] update docs: security compliance section and migration guide

What changed (high level):
- runtime/audit/presence_stamp.go: new package that constructs an HMAC-SHA256 stamp over (request_id | lease_id | key_id | timestamp). The stamp and the constituent metadata are emitted as structured audit headers (X-RW-Audit-Stamp, X-RW-Audit-Meta) for downstream ingestion.
- runtime/operator/session.go: ensure operator lease id is attached to inbound requests from operator-facing routes and forwarded through internal RPC.
- runtime/kms/router.go: new ConsentGatedRouter that prefers region-local CMKs. If a local key is unavailable, the router consults the tenant's consent claims (stored in the claims service) before routing to a multi-region key. Consent is stored as a signed claim with an expiration to avoid long-lived overrides.
- tools/rbacctl/validate.go: CLI that lints RBACv2 rules, flags mismatches between shadow and enforce sets, and simulates decision outcomes for a small queries corpus.
- deploy/migrations/2026-02-25-rbac-shadow-to-enforce.sh: migration helper to snapshot current shadow policies, generate diffs, and produce a staged rollout plan (canary cohorts by tenant tag).
- docs/security/migration_rbacv2_adoption.md: migration guide and rollback playbook.

Review conversation (high level):
- Eric Huang (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end here. Two asks: (1) can you include a note on threat model for the presence stamp and where we trust HMAC keys? (2) prefer the consent claim TTL be configurable via tenancy settings rather than hardcoded 90d."
- Author (Lena): "Thanks, Eric. Added threat model section to docs and make TTL configurable via tenant config with default 90d; see services/claims/consent_store.go change."
- Priya Nair (reviewer): "rbacctl validate is great. Please make sure policy diffs include an example JSON output for automations. Also add an option to simulate a small traffic sample."
- Author: "Added --json-output flag and a --simulate-sample-size option. Updated README for rbacctl."
- Tomás Varela (security reviewer): "Concern about exposing key_id in logs; recommend key_id be redacted unless the request comes from an auditor role. Also verify stamps cannot be replayed."
- Author: "Applied role-gated redaction for key_id in the audit pipeline and added nonce+timestamp into the stamp input to reduce replay risk. Integration tests added to ensure replay attempts are rejected."

CI and checks summary:
- CI run 1 (2026-02-22): unit tests failing (lint warnings + one race in presence_stamp_test)
- CI run 2 (2026-02-24): fixed lint failures, addressed race; integration matrix started, two flaky tests disabled with tracked tickets.
- CI run 3 (2026-02-27): full matrix passed (unit + integration + e2e smoke), codecov decreased by 0.3% due to migration script docs; flagged as acceptable.

Merge notes: After approvals from Eric, Priya and Tomás and one successful full CI run, the PR was squashed and merged to main on 2026-03-01 by Eric Huang. Post-merge actions:
- Ops: rollout plan executed in three phases; initial canary (10 tenants) then 100 then full.
- Compliance: auditors received a short brief and the migration guide.
- Monitoring: added a temporary anomaly alert to detect increased KMS cross-region traffic.

Migration and rollback guidance:
- Use deploy/migrations/2026-02-25-rbac-shadow-to-enforce.sh to preview diffs and generate canary lists.
- If you observe an unexpected deny spike, revert enforcement by flipping tenant cohort back to shadow via rbacctl set-mode <tenant> shadow.

Other notes:
- This PR intentionally keeps the presence stamp HMAC keys in the platform KMS; we plan to introduce an HSM-backed signer in a follow-up.
- We intentionally do not add key_id to plaintext user-facing logs; only auditors with the "security:read_audit_key" role can see the unredacted key_id in the audit UI.
